clue.text: Sleep indecently with hem wrapped round her bottom? Au contraire!

indicators.note: doing something indecently means behaving improperly, so these letters lose their proper order
a wrapping goes all the way round its contents, so one string encloses another

blocks.note: French for 'on the contrary': swap each word for its opposite, her to his and bottom to top

explanation.surface: A cheeky boudoir scene: someone sleeping in a racy fashion with a hemline pulled round her backside.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble says four answers are undefined; all four are names for the Devil. 'Au contraire!' tells you to reverse the sense of 'her bottom', which becomes HIS TOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Mephistopheles is the demon of the Faust legend, a recognised name for Satan, so he belongs among the four devilish solutions.

clue.text: One power-hungry Arab enters a new calm age

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so one piece sits within the other
something made new has been remade, so these letters take a fresh order

blocks.note: an Omani is an Arab from Oman

explanation.surface: A greedy Arab ruler bursts into a peaceful new era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arab' is not the definition here; it supplies a nationality word that sits inside the reworked letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A megalomaniac is a person obsessed with wielding power and control, exactly someone with an appetite for domination.

clue.text: 13 form pressure flap

indicators.note: split it as 'for M': one letter is put in place of that letter

blocks.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Reads like a technical note about a pressure-operated flap on some machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' must be split into 'for M', so P replaces the M of MANIC. Bloggers flagged this split as a stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A flap is a state of agitated nervous alarm, an informal British sense matching sudden fear.

clue.text: Couch stuffing controversial topic, actually

indicators.note: stuffing is packed inside something, so one piece goes into another
something controversial stirs things up, so these letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: A sofa-side debate: a contentious subject turns out to be what is really padding the couch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couch' looks like a verb meaning to phrase something, but it is the piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Ipso facto is Latin for 'by that very fact', loosely used to mean in reality or as a matter of fact.

clue.text: Pointed exchange between sections of bureaucracy

indicators.note: parts trading places means the two halves swap ends

explanation.surface: A barbed memo passed between two departments of the civil service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointed exchange' reads as a sharp argument, but 'Pointed' stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tapered narrows gradually to a point, so it is pointed in shape.

clue.text: Supports lip-refashioning treatment finally covered by NHS

indicators.note: to refashion is to remake in a new shape, so these letters change order
finally points to the end, so only the closing letter is kept
something covered sits underneath and inside, so one piece is enclosed by another

explanation.surface: A complaint that the health service pays for cosmetic lip surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's National Health Service. The final letter of treatment sits between its first and second letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Plinths are the stone or wooden bases on which statues and columns rest, so they hold them up.

clue.text: Hammer squared might follow said host

indicators.note: something said is spoken, so we want the spelling of a spoken form

blocks.note: MC Hammer is the American rapper, so his title is MC

explanation.surface: A physics joke: Einstein's E equals MC squared, with the rapper Hammer standing in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hammer squared' evokes MC squared, which follows E in Einstein's formula. Spoken, MC is the word for a compere.
explanation.definitionFit: An emcee is a master of ceremonies, the person who introduces acts and presents an event.

clue.text: Best hotel price had uncovered secrets

indicators.note: with the covers taken off, each word loses its outer letters and keeps its inside

explanation.surface: An exposé: someone has revealed the hidden secrets of getting the best hotel rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncovered secrets' reads as revealed secrets, but 'uncovered' works on each of the four words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoterica are matters understood only by a small initiated circle, obscure lore kept from outsiders.

clue.text: Loon gets out

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or not right, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: once the first three letters have served as the definition, the stray final letter remains

explanation.surface: A crazy person is released from somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loon' must be split into LOO plus N, an unusual trick. A loo is a British toilet; the gents is a men's public lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: The gents is British slang for a men's public toilet, so it is one kind of lavatory.

clue.text: At last, reduction in night tariff?

indicators.note: at last points to the end of a word, so only its final letter is used
in places one thing inside another

explanation.surface: A hopeful question about whether off-peak electricity is finally getting cheaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble leaves this undefined; it is one of four names for the Devil. One letter dropped into PRICE turns it into PRINCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince of Darkness is a traditional title for Satan, ruler of the forces of evil.

clue.text: Pastille chez Google? Un problème

indicators.note: French for a problem; letters in trouble get thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Mock French: a sweet at the Google office, and a problem with it.
explanation.walkthrough: The French dresses the clue up, but 'Un' is fodder and only 'problème' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastille is a small medicated sweet sucked to soothe a sore throat, which is what a cough lozenge is.

clue.text: Something filthy with twisted tail provided on board

indicators.note: a twisted end is turned about, so the closing pair of letters swaps round
whatever is on board is carried inside the vessel, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: from the phrase 'filthy lucre', meaning money

explanation.surface: A dirty creature with a curly tail is allowed onto a ship, like a stowaway rat.
explanation.walkthrough: Undefined by the preamble; Lucifer is a name for the Devil. 'Something filthy' leads to LUCRE through the stock phrase 'filthy lucre'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucifer, the fallen light-bearing angel, is a traditional biblical name for Satan.

clue.text: Another Etonian's got to it

indicators.note: what a phrase has got is held within it, so the letters lie in the run of words

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A second Old Etonian has made it to some position, a jibe at public-school privilege.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is an elite English boarding school, so an Etonian is one of its pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereto is a formal adverb meaning to that thing, used in legal or official writing.

clue.text: Lodge may be not so hectic

indicators.note: not excludes something, so a pair of letters is taken away

blocks.note: a Masonic lodge is a branch of the Freemasons
taken as written, to be removed

explanation.surface: Someone hopes a country lodge will be a calmer, less frantic place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not so hectic' looks like a phrase meaning calm, but 'not so' removes letters and 'hectic' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Manic means frenzied and frantically busy, the same as a hectic schedule or pace.

clue.text: Young King Edward may be getting partners on vessel into alliance

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece sits on top of the next
going into something puts it inside, so one piece is enclosed

blocks.note: East and West are partners at the bridge table
the North Atlantic Treaty Organization is a military alliance

explanation.surface: A young royal pictured taking partners aboard a ship to join an alliance.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward is a popular British potato variety, not a monarch; an early-season one is a new potato.
explanation.definitionFit: A new potato is a young, freshly dug potato, and King Edward is an example variety.

clue.text: Crippling debt in such a bank loan, interest not greedy to begin with

indicators.note: what comes to begin with is at the start, so the opening letter of each word is kept

explanation.surface: Crushing debt from a bank loan, though the interest rate was not greedy at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crippling debt' reads as a single phrase, but 'Crippling' alone is the definition and 'debt' starts the run of initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Disabling means causing incapacity or severe damage, the same as crippling in both literal and figurative use.

clue.text: BBC coverage of central Highlands cattle

indicators.note: coverage wraps around something, so one piece encloses others
central points to the very middle, so only the midpoint letter is taken

blocks.note: the Beeb is the BBC's British nickname

explanation.surface: A television listing for a BBC programme about Highland cattle in central Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Undefined by the preamble; Beelzebub is a name for the Devil. The BBC is known in Britain as the Beeb.
explanation.definitionFit: Beelzebub, the biblical 'lord of the flies', is a traditional name for Satan or a chief demon.

clue.text: Magazine never lost heart to Corbyn's penultimate position in Labour

indicators.note: penultimate means second to last, so just that letter is kept
to position something in a place is to set it inside
losing a heart to something means the middle is given up and replaced by it

blocks.note: taken as written; its middle letter goes

explanation.surface: A political jibe about Jeremy Corbyn, then Labour Party leader, and a magazine that has never lost faith.
explanation.walkthrough: Capitalised 'Labour' suggests the British political party, but here it simply means work. The V at the centre of NEVER is swapped out.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Yorker is a long-running American weekly magazine of journalism, fiction and cartoons.

clue.text: Look up Her Majesty's Custodians

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: to peek is to take a quick look
ER is the Queen, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: An instruction to search for royal guardians, perhaps at the Tower of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look up' reads as one verb meaning to research, but 'up' turns the look round.
explanation.definitionFit: Keepers are people charged with guarding or caring for something, which is what custodians do.

clue.text: Mature about East German comeback

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: Ost is the German word for east

explanation.surface: An ageing East German athlete mounting a sporting return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East German' suggests the old GDR, but it means the word for east in German.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick, sharp reply, the kind of witty retort also called a comeback.

clue.text: The kind of communication that gives compiler back trouble

indicators.note: going back means running the other way, so the letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: the compiler is the setter, who refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: The setter grumbling that a particular kind of message gives him back pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back trouble' looks like a sore spine, but 'back' works on the setter and 'trouble' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Email is a form of electronic communication, sent as messages between computers.

clue.text: Follower runs back into safety location

indicators.note: the letters sit right inside the clue's words
running back means going the other way, so the letters read from right to left

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A devotee retreats to a safe spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs' looks like it should be R, the cricket abbreviation, but it is part of the signal that the letters read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An acolyte is a devoted assistant or disciple, someone who follows a leader.

clue.text: Part of a shirt left rustic

blocks.note: the yoke is the shaped panel across a shirt's shoulders
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A piece of shirt fabric left looking homespun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rustic' reads as an adjective describing the shirt, but it is a noun meaning a country person.
explanation.definitionFit: A yokel is an unsophisticated country dweller, which is what a rustic is as a noun.

clue.text: After food, sound sleeping produces vigour

indicators.note: after places one piece following the other in order

blocks.note: ZZ is the cartoon snoring noise of a sleeper

explanation.surface: Health advice: eat well, sleep soundly and you will feel full of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound sleeping' reads as deep sleep, but it is the noise a sleeper makes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pizzazz is lively energy and flair, a colloquial word for vitality or zest.

clue.text: Fiddle in!

blocks.note: surface reading: a cheery call to start playing the violin, or to join in
setter's reading: look for a violin maker's name inside the word for the closing punctuation mark

explanation.walkthrough: An indirect hidden word: the letters are not in the clue but in the name of the mark that ends it. Bloggers called it sneaky.
explanation.definitionFit: An Amati is a violin by the Amati family of Cremona, and fiddle is the informal word for violin.

clue.text: See 9
Basin emptied and filled with uncooked beef

indicators.note: something emptied has lost its contents, so only the outer letters remain
being filled with something means holding it inside

explanation.surface: A kitchen scene: a bowl tipped out, then loaded up with raw meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncooked beef' looks like one item, but 'beef' stands alone as the definition in its sense of muscle.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef in its slang sense means muscular strength, and brawn is physical power or muscle.

clue.text: One must be sensible with logo design

indicators.note: design means a new arrangement, so these letters are laid out afresh

explanation.surface: Branding advice: a logo should be designed with good sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One must be sensible' reads as a single maxim, but the definition stops at 'must'.
explanation.definitionFit: Noblesse oblige is the principle that privilege brings duty: the aristocrat is obliged, so one must act honourably.
